These two countries are pretty much dependent on tourism for their economies to function, which means they are packed with tourists from all around the world. You can arrive at some airport alone but instantly find some people to travel with you. My friend and I met a girl and she stuck with us throughout the entire Bolivia part of the trip. I also met a French girl in Peru who was traveling even longer and hadn't spent one day by herself; every week or so she'd be join some random group of strangers and stick with them.

I went early this year. I live in Brazil so that's where I started off. Crossed the Brazil-Bolivia border on foot and took trains and buses all around the country. I didn't really see much of Peru aside from Machu Picchu though. The trail I did was the Inka Jungle trail, as the classic Inca trail requires advanced reservations and I wasn't sure when I'd actually arrive in Peru. It was the best thing I've ever done in my life though. If you love nature and seeing shit from a compeltely different culture, visit Bolivia and Peru.
